theory.intro: Each neighbouring pair of mass units is linked by a factor of $1000$: tonnes to kilograms, and kilograms to grams. Convert one link at a time by multiplying or dividing by $1000$.
facts: Going to a **smaller** unit (kg→g, t→kg): **multiply** by $1000$.
Going to a **larger** unit (g→kg, kg→t): **divide** by $1000$.
steps: Identify the starting and requested units. Use $1\text{ t}=1000\text{ kg}$ and $1\text{ kg}=1000\text{ g}$.
For each link, multiply by $1000$ to use the smaller unit or divide by $1000$ to use the larger unit. Keep zeros in empty places. For tonnes and grams, use both links through kilograms.

workedExamples.question_text:
Convert to the smaller unit.
(a) $2.483$ kg to grams
(b) $3.067$ t to kilograms

Convert to the larger unit.
(a) $74$ g to kilograms
(b) $83$ kg to tonnes
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $74\div1000=0.074$.
$74\text{ g}=0.074\text{ kg}$.
(b) $83\div1000=0.083$.
$83\text{ kg}=0.083\text{ t}$.
Use zeros to hold the empty tenths places.

workedExamples.question_text:
Write each mass in grams.
(a) $2.057$ kg
(b) $0.014$ t
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Convert kilograms to grams.
$2.057\times1000=2057$.
$2.057\text{ kg}=2057\text{ g}$.
(b) Convert tonnes to kilograms first.
$0.014\times1000=14$, so $0.014\text{ t}=14\text{ kg}$.
Then convert kilograms to grams.
$14\times1000=14000$.
$0.014\text{ t}=14000\text{ g}$.

Convert grams to kilograms first.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}768\,000\div1000\\&=768\end{aligned}$
$768\,000\text{ g}=768\text{ kg}$.
Then convert kilograms to tonnes.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}768\div1000\\&=0.768\end{aligned}$
$768\,000\text{ g}=0.768\text{ t}$.
